question: When a Judge of a High Court in India, including the Chief Justice, wishes to resign from office, to whom must they submit their resignation?

options.text: The Governor of the respective state

solution:
The correct answer is __**The President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Judge of a High Court in India, including the Chief Justice, submits their resignation to **The President of India**.
 
• The resignation must be in writing, addressed formally to the President, as per **Article 217(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• The process ensures accountability and adherence to constitutional protocols regarding judicial appointments and resignations.
 
• High Court Judges hold office until the age of 62 years or until resignation, removal, or transfer as per constitutional provisions.
 
• The President acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers while accepting the resignation of a High Court Judge.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 217 of the Indian Constitution**

 
 
• It deals with the appointment and conditions of service of High Court Judges.
 
• It specifies the qualifications for becoming a High Court Judge, including being a citizen of India and having at least 10 years of judicial experience.
 
• It covers provisions related to resignation, removal, and transfer of High Court Judges.
 
 
 
• **Removal of High Court Judges**
 
 
• Judges can be removed through a process called impeachment, as per **Article 124(4)** and **Article 217(1)(b)**.
 
• The process requires a majority vote in Parliament based on proven misconduct or incapacity.
 
 
 
• **Transfer of High Court Judges**
 
 
• Under **Article 222**, the President has the power to transfer a High Court Judge after consultation with the Chief Justice of India.
 
• Transfers are made to ensure better administration of justice or to fill vacancies in other High Courts.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Chief Justice of India (CJI)**
 
 
• The CJI plays a crucial advisory role in matters related to the appointment, transfer, and removal of High Court Judges.
 
• This ensures a transparent and balanced approach to judicial administration.
